info.name: Leadership Intelligence Scoring Engine
info.description: Every endpoint of the API. Start the stack with `docker compose up -d --build`, then run folder 1 top to bottom. Tokens come from the local mock identity provider (client_id = persona: owner, admin, leader, analyst, viewer, org1-viewer, other-admin). Change the collection variable "persona" to act as another role.

exec: // Fetches (and caches) a token from the local mock identity provider for the persona in use.
// Persona: header X-Persona on the request (removed before sending), else the collection variable "persona".
if (cached && Date.now() < exp) { pm.variables.set('accessToken', cached); return; }
if (err || res.code !== 200) { throw new Error('token request failed for persona ' + persona + ': ' + (err || res.text())); }

request.description: Server generates the assessmentId and stores an immutable snapshot. Optional header Idempotency-Key. Roles: OWNER, ADMIN, ENGINEERING_LEADER. Saves assessmentId and scoringRunId.

exec: pm.test('carries the diagnostic notice', () => pm.expect(b.notice).to.include('not an individual performance rating'));

request.description: Coverage below the configured requirement gives scoreStatus INSUFFICIENT_DATA, never an invented score.

item.name: Calculate with member answers (organization and team results)

request.description: Answers carry a scope (D45): MEMBER (one respondent, no identity), TEAM or ORGANIZATION. The response is the organization run (all answers pooled) with teamRuns; a team with fewer answers than the configured minimum (default 5) has no score. Send inputs or responses, never both. Saves scopedRunId and teamRunId.

exec: pm.test('organization result with two team results', () => { pm.expect(b.scope).to.eql('ORGANIZATION'); pm.expect(b.teamRuns.length).to.eql(2); });

request.description: A team run reads like any run, with scope TEAM, its teamId and organizationScoringRunId. It is never part of history, trends, the dashboard or comparison.

exec: pm.test('team scope', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.scope).to.eql('TEAM'); pm.expect(b.teamId).to.eql('alpha'); });
